name: TabPFN-3
developer: Prior Labs GmbH (Grinsztajn, Flöge, Key, Birkel, Jund, Roof, Manium, Hoo, Bühler, Garg, Safaric, Robertson, Jäger, ... Hollmann, Hutter; 41 authors)

availability.notes: Weights are downloadable from Hugging Face but gated: the tabpfn package (>=8.0.0) opens a Prior Labs login on first use and requires one-time acceptance of the TABPFN-3 License (or a TABPFN_TOKEN API key for headless use); offline use is possible after caching the .ckpt files [S4,S9,S12]. Inference code is open source in the tabpfn package; only fine-tuning code is included, not the pre-training code or the synthetic prior generator [S4,S5]. Hosted inference via the Prior Labs API / tabpfn-client (free tier, token-metered) and enterprise/VPC deployments (AWS SageMaker, Azure AI Foundry, Databricks, SAP); TabPFN-3-Plus (native text) and TabPFN-3-Plus (Thinking) are API/enterprise-only [S1,S3,S10]. TabPFN-3 was the default model of tabpfn 8.0.0 (2026-05-12) until tabpfn 9.0.0 (2026-09-15) made TabPFN-3.5 the default; TabPFN-3 remains selectable via ModelVersion.V3 [S5,S6]. Released checkpoints: tabpfn-v3-classifier-v3_default.ckpt and tabpfn-v3-regressor-v3_default.ckpt plus six experimental variants (20260417 binary/multiclass classifiers, 20260417 mediumdata regressor, 20260506 OOD classifier/regressor, 20260506 timeseries regressor = TabPFN-TS-3) [S7].

license.code: Apache-2.0 (since tabpfn 9.0.0, 2026-09-15); at the TabPFN-3 release (tabpfn 8.0.0) the repository was under the 'Prior Labs License' v1.2 = Apache 2.0 with an additional attribution provision (Paragraph 10, Llama-3 style)
license.weights: TABPFN-3 License v1.0 (Prior Labs GmbH, last revised 2026-03-24; called 'TABPFN-3.0 License v1.0' in the report) - a non-commercial, non-production licence
license.prior_or_data: not applicable: the synthetic prior generator and pre-training data/code are not released (proprietary); the licence covers weights, parameters and inference code only
license.notes: Weights licence text [S8]: non-exclusive, revocable, royalty-free licence 'solely for your Non-Commercial Purposes' = testing, evaluation or research not tied to commercial gain, production deployment or revenue generation, incl. internal benchmarking, academic research, experimentation on private/public data and public data-science competitions (Kaggle etc.). Explicitly NOT permitted without a commercial licence: any revenue-generating activity, production systems or end-user interactions, client deliverables, using results in commercial decision-making (incl. procurement/vendor benchmarking and proof-of-value), hosting the model as a paid or free API/SaaS/managed service, and training/fine-tuning/distilling other models for commercial use. Outputs may only be used non-commercially; derivatives (fine-tunes) inherit all restrictions; redistribution must carry the licence and an attribution notice; further bans on military, surveillance and biometric use; not available to consumers (Sec. 13 BGB, proof of business status may be requested); German law, Berlin courts. Code licence is separate: Apache-2.0 today (Prior Labs License v1.2 at release) [S4,S5,S6]. Prior Labs' docs FAQ confirms enterprises may only run preliminary internal evaluations; production, product integration or business decisions need a Commercial Enterprise License or the API [S10]. TabArena registers the model with commercial_use=False, license='TabPFN-3 License v1.0 (non-commercial)' [S15]. Commercial licensing: sales@priorlabs.ai; the hosted API is governed by Prior Labs' general terms instead of this licence [S8].

architecture.type: three-stage row-compression in-context-learning transformer (TabICLv2-style: column-wise inducing-point feature-distribution embedding -> row-wise CLS-token feature aggregation -> row-level ICL transformer) with an attention-based many-class retrieval decoder
architecture.parameters_note: 53 M parameters for the classifier and 58 M for the regressor (Fig. 4 table of the report [S1]); the two checkpoints share all hyperparameters except the task-specific output decoder. HF checkpoint files: classifier 212.8 MB, regressor 233.3 MB [S7]. For comparison the report lists TabPFN-2.5 at 11 M (clf) / 10 M (reg) and TabPFN-2.6 at 11 M / 13 M.
architecture.layers: 3 column-wise induced-self-attention blocks (feature distribution embedding) + 3 row-wise transformer blocks (feature aggregation) + 24 ICL transformer blocks; classifier adds a 1-layer attention retrieval decoder (6 heads x 64), regressor a 2-layer MLP head (512 -> 1024 -> 5000)
architecture.attention_scheme: Base embedding dimension 128; each row is compressed into 4 CLS tokens whose concatenation gives the 512-dim row embedding used by the ICL stage (icl_emsize = 128 x 4). Stage 1 (per column, in parallel or column-chunked): induced self-attention with 128 inducing points and 8 heads, avoiding quadratic cross-row attention. Stage 2 (per row): non-causal attention among the row's grouped feature embeddings and 4 learned CLS tokens, with RoPE (base 100,000). Stage 3 (ICL): training rows use full multi-head self-attention (8 query heads, 8 KV heads); test rows attend to training rows with multi-query cross-attention using a single KV head, shrinking the KV cache 8x. Stages 1 and 3 and the decoder use the query-aware scalable softmax (QASSMax, from TabICLv2) for length generalisation to large training sets. RMSNorm everywhere; feed-forward expansion factor 2. FlashAttention-3 is auto-selected for the ICL attention on Hopper GPUs (SDPA elsewhere, MATH fallback on T4-class GPUs) [S1,S5].
architecture.checkpoints: separate classification & regression checkpoints (identical backbone hyperparameters, different output decoder) plus experimental specialised variants (binary, multiclass, medium-data regression, out-of-distribution classifier/regressor, time-series regressor = TabPFN-TS-3) [S7]
architecture.regression_head: distributional: bar-distribution (Riemann) head with 5000 buckets produced by a 2-layer GELU MLP (512 -> 1024 -> 5000); arbitrary quantiles/CDF decoded from one forward pass; full predictive distribution exposed by the package (predict quantiles, pdf)
architecture.feature_embedding: Features are mean-imputed/standardised, then grouped into triplets with two cyclically shifted neighbours (TabICLv2 grouping, circular shifts (0,1,3), feature_group_size=3); each triplet is concatenated with a 3-dim NaN/Inf indicator mask and linearly projected (3+3 -> 128) into a cell embedding. Training-row cells receive target-aware label embeddings (learned embeddings initialised via orthogonal decomposition, near-maximally separated for up to 160 classes; separate tables for the column encoder and the ICL stage). Columns are then summarised by the inducing-point distribution embedder and rows by 4 CLS tokens [S1].
key_innovations: Return from TabPFN-2.x's alternating row/feature attention to TabPFN-v1-style ICL over whole-row embeddings, using TabICLv2's two-stage row compression so the ICL cost scales with n_train^2 independent of the number of features (enables 1M training rows on one GPU)

Attention-based many-class retrieval decoder: class probabilities are a head-averaged attention-weighted average of in-context one-hot labels (soft nearest-neighbour retrieval), permutation-equivariant in class indices and non-parametric in the class count; trained with a hard ceiling of 160 classes fixed by the label-embedding tensors

Row-chunking: two-phase exactly-equivalent inference (inducing states computed once over the full training set, then rows streamed through embedding stages in fixed chunks) that decouples peak activation memory from rows x columns (~5x lower peak memory, enabled when n_train + n_test > 2048)

Reduced KV cache via multi-query test-to-train attention (one KV head) plus caching only inducing states, per-layer train K/V and final train embeddings: ~7 GiB per estimator at 1M rows; cached predict 1-3 orders of magnitude faster than cold fit+predict
Orthogonally initialised target embeddings, RMSNorm instead of LayerNorm, explicit NaN/Inf indicator inputs (native missing-value handling), QASSMax scalable softmax in all attention stages

Improved preprocessing: round-robin/balanced feature subsampling so every feature appears in at least one estimator (<=200 features per estimator), Gini-importance (LightGBM) feature selection for datasets >100k rows, GPU-side quantile normalisation/SVD/squashing scaler, auto-scaled n_estimators for very wide tables

Substantially extended SCM prior (new DAG samplers, combiner mechanisms, categorical model, high-frequency sinusoidal activations, spatial activations, many-class targets, discrete-time dynamic-SCM temporal prior, out-of-distribution/extrapolation tasks) trained on >8 trillion tokens
Opt-in torch.compile (up to 1.58x on MI-250x) and FlashAttention-3 (1.5-1.7x at 1M rows on H100) backends; distillation into dataset-specific MLPs/tree ensembles (enterprise engine)
Test-time compute scaling ('Thinking mode', API-only TabPFN-3-Plus) introduced for tabular foundation models; native text features in TabPFN-3-Plus

capabilities.max_classes_note: Native support for up to 160 classes (hard ceiling fixed at pre-training through the orthogonal label-embedding tensors and the decoder's one-hot value tensor; previous versions: 10) [S1,S9,S10]. More classes via the ManyClassClassifier ECOC extension in tabpfn-extensions (a 5,000-class problem needs ~32 sub-fits with the 160-symbol alphabet) [S13]. TabArena's wrapper sets max_classes=160 [S15].
capabilities.max_features_note: Documented model ceiling: 2,000 columns (docs Models page and HF card: 'up to 1M samples and <=2000 features'; rows and columns trade off) [S7,S10]. The report's benchmark-validated SOTA envelope is a cell budget: 1M rows x 200 features, 100k rows x 2,000 features, or 1k rows x 20,000 features [S1]. Each estimator sees at most 200 features by default; wider tables are covered by feature subsampling across estimators (round-robin, or Gini-importance top-k for >100k rows) with n_estimators auto-scaled so every feature is used (32 estimators used on the 1,117-22,215-feature slice) [S1,S5]. ignore_pretraining_limits=True lifts the package guardrail.
capabilities.max_samples_note: Up to 1,000,000 training rows in-context (10x TabPFN-2.5); validated at 1M rows x 200 features on a single 80 GiB H100 using row-chunking (with KV cache also at 1M) [S1,S9,S10]. Large-data benchmarks cover 100k-1M rows; the HF card notes performance is not guaranteed above 1M rows or >2,000 features [S7]. CPU inference is capped by the package at 5,000 samples for TabPFN-3 (1,000 for older versions; override with TABPFN_ALLOW_CPU_LARGE_DATASET) [S4]. Hosted API: 1M rows for TabPFN-3/TabPFN-3-Plus, 200k rows for TabPFN-3-Thinking [S10]. Optional per-estimator row subsampling via inference_config SUBSAMPLE_SAMPLES (stratified for classification) [S5,S9].
capabilities.categorical_features: handled natively by the built-in preprocessing pipeline (categorical strings/categories auto-detected or passed via categorical_features_indices; no manual encoding needed); the SCM prior's categorical-variable model was reworked for TabPFN-3 [S1,S9]
capabilities.other: Open-source model: numerical + categorical + missing values only; text columns need the API-only TabPFN-3-Plus. Full predictive distributions/quantiles from the bar-distribution head; KV-cached inference (fit_mode='fit_with_cache') for repeated predictions and fast SHAP via shapiq; row embeddings extraction (output of the ICL stage); gradient-based fine-tuning (FinetunedTabPFNClassifier/Regressor); post-processing with decision-threshold tuning (e.g. F1) and temperature scaling, balance_probabilities for imbalanced data; distillation into MLPs/tree ensembles (enterprise); time-series forecasting via the TabPFN-TS-3 checkpoint (tabpfn-time-series); relational data via TabPFN-REL / RDBLearn; causal T/S/X meta-learners; extrapolation with the OOD checkpoints; multi-GPU parallelisation of estimators [S1,S4,S9,S10].

pretraining.synthetic_prior_summary: Structural-causal-model (SCM) prior, extended from TabPFN-2.5: (1) sample dataset hyper-parameters (rows N, features P, classes C, ...); (2) sample a DAG with new graph-sampling algorithms for richer structural diversity; (3) draw i.i.d. noise per node and compute the SCM in topological order, combining parent values through a host of new 'combiner mechanisms' and activations (incl. improved sinusoidal activations for high-frequency oscillations and spatial activations encoding lon/lat- or sensor-grid-like structure); (4) pick feature and target nodes; (5) post-process. New in TabPFN-3: a more expressive categorical-variable model, a many-class prior (binary up to hundreds of classes) matching the retrieval decoder, a temporal prior extending the SCM to a discrete-time Dynamic SCM (rows collected over time, time-ordered train/test splits), and an out-of-distribution prior with extrapolation tasks. The final model was trained on more than 8 trillion tokens of such synthetic data; no real data. Number of datasets, tokens-per-dataset and the exact hyper-parameter ranges are not disclosed [S1].
pretraining.num_synthetic_datasets_note: not stated; the report only says the final model 'was trained on more than 8 trillion tokens' (the notion of token is not defined, presumably table cells) [S1]
pretraining.real_data: none: 'pretrained exclusively on synthetic data from our prior'; the TabPFN-TS-3 checkpoint is fine-tuned on synthetic time-series data, and Thinking mode uses no LLMs, real data or internet search [S1,S7]
pretraining.objective: not stated in the report (no loss function is given; the regressor's 5000-bucket bar distribution implies a discretised distributional target, and the classifier decoder outputs log-probabilities, but the training loss itself is not documented)
pretraining.hardware: not stated explicitly; the acknowledgements credit EuroHPC access to the LUMI supercomputer (CSC, Finland; AMD MI250X GPUs) and inference measurements are reported on AMD MI-250x, H100 and RTX Pro 6000 [S1]
pretraining.compute: not stated (only '>8 trillion tokens' of training data)
pretraining.training_cost_note: No GPU-hours, wall-clock time or cost disclosed for pre-training; the only compute-related statements are the LUMI acknowledgement and the 8T-token figure [S1].

icl.context_note: The whole training set is used as context (no default row subsampling): the ICL stage attends over one 512-dim embedding per row, so context scales to 1M rows on a single 80 GiB H100 (with row-chunking; also with KV cache) [S1]. Rows and columns trade off (1M x 200, 100k x 2,000, 1k x 20,000 validated) [S1]. Optional per-estimator subsampling via inference_config SUBSAMPLE_SAMPLES (docs suggest 100,000 for very large tables; stratified round-robin pools for the classifier) [S5,S9]. Time-series: up to 32k historical steps of context in the fev-bench evaluation [S1].
icl.large_dataset_strategy: row-chunking (stream rows through feature-embedding and aggregation stages in fixed chunks reusing pre-computed inducing states; exact, enabled when n_train + n_test > 2048) plus column-chunking of the inducing-state computation; GPU preprocessing; Gini-importance feature selection per estimator above 100k rows; <=200 features per estimator; optional SUBSAMPLE_SAMPLES; test rows batched (TabArena batches above 150k rows; cached inference chunks test rows at 32,768); estimators can be parallelised over multiple GPUs; KV cache to amortise the training-set pass [S1,S4,S5,S15]
icl.test_time_ensembling: 8 estimators by default (n_estimators=8), each with a different dataset/feature permutation and feature transformation (robust scaling + soft clipping, quantile transform, standard scaling, some with SVD components) and its own <=200-feature subset; n_estimators is auto-scaled so every feature is covered; TabArena Pareto variants N1/N2/N4 use 1/2/4 estimators; 32 estimators on the many-features slice [S1,S5]
icl.fine_tuning: Supported in the open-source package: FinetunedTabPFNClassifier / FinetunedTabPFNRegressor (gradient-based, optional fixed preprocessing seed, distributes across GPUs with torchrun); recommended for >1000 rows, niche domains or families of related tables. TabPFN-TS-3 is such a fine-tuned checkpoint. Fine-tuned derivatives stay under the non-commercial licence. Test-time compute scaling ('Thinking mode', extra fit-time optimisation) exists only for the API model TabPFN-3-Plus [S1,S9,S10,S14].
icl.inference_notes: KV cache ~7 GiB per estimator at 1M rows (~56 GiB for the default 8 estimators); on an H100 cached predict takes 0.1-3 ms per test point (batches of 100) and is 1-3 orders of magnitude faster than the cold fit+predict path; building the cache costs the same as a cold fit+predict (~107 s at n_train = 1e6 for a single estimator without preprocessing) [S1]. Docs claim predictions in under 0.2 ms per row on 1M rows [S9]. FlashAttention-3 gives 1.49-1.73x at 1M rows on H100; torch.compile up to 1.58x on MI-250x [S1]. Distillation into dataset-specific MLP/tree ensembles for CPU sub-millisecond latency is an enterprise feature [S1]. Managed API supports KV caching only for TabPFN-3 and later, max 10,000 test rows per cached predict call [S11].

speed.hardware_note: Report inference measurements: NVIDIA H100 80 GiB (chunking, KV cache, FA3), AMD MI-250x (torch.compile), RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell (SHAP); TabArena numbers in the report were produced on a single RTX 6000 GPU (other foundation models on H200) [S1]. Docs: minimum NVIDIA T4, A100/H100 recommended; CPU/MPS only for small data [S12].
speed.memory_note: Row-chunking flattens peak memory w.r.t. feature count (~5x reduction at the largest shapes) and lets 1M rows x 200 features fit on one 80 GiB H100; KV cache ~7 GiB per estimator at 1M rows; regressor peak memory reduced ~60% at large test sets (57.6 -> 22.8 GB at n_test = 250k) [S1,S5]. README: ~8 GB VRAM suffices for many datasets, 16 GB for some large ones; TabArena assumes a 10 GB GPU baseline [S4,S15].
speed.speed_claims: Up to 20x faster than TabPFN-2.5 (largest gains at high feature counts) [S1]; TabArena (report Table 8): median train 2.31 s and predict 0.74 s per 1K rows for TabPFN-3 (D) vs 5.81 s / 0.64 s for RealTabPFN-2.5 (D) and 289 s / 4.03 s for AutoGluon 1.5 extreme [S1]; KV-cached predict 1-3 orders of magnitude faster than cold inference [S1]; SHAP via shapiq >120x faster with the KV cache (1.08 s per test row for a 200k x 500 table) [S1]; TabPFN-3-Plus (Thinking) beats AutoGluon 1.5 extreme (4h) in under a tenth of its runtime [S1]; docs: <0.2 ms per prediction on 1M rows [S9].
speed.inference_cost_note: Local inference is free under the non-commercial licence. Hosted API (tabpfn-client / REST): token-metered; default budgets 5,000,000 tokens/day and 20,000,000 tokens/month, minimum charge 10,000 tokens per billable TabPFN-3/3.5 operation, uploads and standard fits free, predictions and Thinking fits charged (KV-cache reuse is cheaper); rate limits 60 predicts/min (1,500/h), 60 fits/min, 10 Thinking fits/min (30/h), 120 uploads/min [S11]. Commercial/enterprise pricing (API, SageMaker, Azure AI Foundry, on-prem) on request (priorlabs.ai/pricing) [S10].

talent.source: TabPFN-3 technical report, Sec. 3.1.2 (Fig. 13), App. E.3 (Figs. 28-30) - https://arxiv.org/html/2605.13986v2
talent.protocol_note: TabICLv2 evaluation protocol: 274 of the 300 TALENT datasets (the 26 TabPFN-2/TabICLv2 development datasets removed); 64/16/20 train/val/test splits; accuracy for classification, RMSE for regression; mean rank over (dataset, split) pairs with 95% bootstrap CIs (2,000 replicates); baselines are the precomputed TabICLv2-paper results; models capped at 10 classes (TabPFN-2.5, LimiX, TabPFNv2) have the 12 datasets with >10 classes KNN-imputed (4%). Rank values are printed only for TabPFN-3 in the figures (read from the SVG figures).
talent.other: Ranks first overall (mean rank 3.75; next best TabICLv2 at roughly 4.7 and RealTabPFN-2.5 at roughly 5.4, bars unlabelled) and first for every task type (Fig. 28): binary classification 4.08, multiclass 3.30, regression 3.70. Large-rows TALENT slice (14 datasets with 100k-1M training rows, TALENT-provided baselines): mean rank 2.86, first (RealMLP second). Many-class TALENT slice (4 datasets with 100 classes): TabPFN-3 reported as strong (Fig. 29, values not extracted).

other.name: TabArena (report's own run, all 51 datasets / 816 tasks, Elo vs RF=1000)
other.value: TabPFN-3 (D) 1677 (-62/+86), 6.3 wins, improvability 6.9%, train 2.31 s / predict 0.74 s per 1K rows; TabPFN-3-Thinking (API) 1800; AutoGluon 1.5 extreme (4h) 1695; TabPFN-2.6 (D) 1623; RealTabPFN-2.5 (T+E) 1602; TabICLv2 (D) 1599. TabPFN-3 beats RealTabPFN-2.5 (T+E) by 72 Elo; ~80% win rate vs tuned+ensembled CatBoost/LightGBM/XGBoost, 56% vs AutoGluon 1.5 extreme (note: AutoGluon is ranked as a system, so 'first among models' excludes it).

other.name: TabArena-medium (15 largest datasets, 10k-100k rows)
other.value: TabPFN-3 (D) 1835 (-137/+224), improvability 4.1%, train 0.83 s / predict 0.27 s per 1K rows; Thinking 2146; AutoGluon 1.5 extreme 1907; TabPFN-2.6 1741; TabICLv2 1712; RealTabPFN-2.5 (T+E) 1663 (TabPFN-3 ~100 Elo above any other model; Thinking >420 Elo above non-TabPFN models).

other.name: TabArena-small (36 datasets, 500-10k rows)
other.value: TabPFN-3 (D) 1638; AutoGluon 1.5 extreme 1641; Thinking 1723; RealTabPFN-2.5 (T+E) 1598; TabPFN-2.6 1596; TabICLv2 1574

other.name: TabArena-classification (38 datasets) / TabArena-regression (13 datasets)
other.value: classification: TabPFN-3 (D) 1660, Thinking 1782, AutoGluon 1689, TabPFN-2.6 1604; regression: TabPFN-3 (D) 1827, Thinking 1959, AutoGluon 1804, TabPFN-2.6 1776, RealTabPFN-2.5 (T+E) 1774

other.name: Internal large-data benchmark (13 datasets, 100k-1M training rows, <200 features; 9 classification IID, 4 regression with temporal splits)
other.value: TabPFN-3 first: mean rank 2.11 (ROC-AUC, classification) and 2.25 (RMSE, regression) in a single forward pass vs default and 8-hour-tuned XGBoost/CatBoost/LightGBM and TabICLv2 (differences to 8h-tuned XGB/CatBoost not statistically significant); tops normalized scaling curves at 100k/250k/500k/1M rows

other.name: Synthetic many-class benchmark (9 TabArena regression datasets binned into up to 100 classes)
other.value: normalized ROC-AUC (OvR) 1.00 (top-ranked on every dataset/split) vs TabICLv2 0.89 (with many-class wrapper) and TabPFN-2.5 0.83 (ECOC wrapper)

other.name: Quantile regression (TabArena regression datasets, pinball loss over q=0.1..0.9)
other.value: normalized pinball score close to 1.00, first; not significantly different from Quantile TabICLv2, significantly ahead of linear quantile regression, XGBoost-quantile and quantile random forests

other.name: Many-features slice (6 datasets, 102-322 samples, 1,117-22,215 features)
other.value: best normalized ROC-AUC with 32 estimators; Real-TabPFN-2.5 can slightly outperform at equal estimator budget (500 vs 200 features per estimator)

other.name: fev-bench (100 time-series tasks) with TabPFN-TS-3
other.value: SQL skill 43.1% (win rate 73.6%), MASE skill 30.6% (win 69.8%), runtime 234.6 s, 0% leakage - 2nd on both behind Chronos-2 (47.3 / 35.5), ahead of TiRex, TimesFM-2.5, Toto; original TabPFN-v2-TS 39.6 / 27.6 (re-run; 28.8 MASE per fev-bench authors)

other.name: RelBenchV1 (entity classification / regression) with TabPFN-REL and RDBLearn
other.value: TabPFN-REL (built on TabPFN-3) is the best relational foundation model on both tasks (KumoRFMv1/v2 second); supervised RelGNN still best overall; RDBLearn with fixed TabPFN-3 backend beats vanilla RDBLearn (best open-source RFM). Per-dataset numbers in Tables 14-15.

other.name: TabSTAR text-tabular collection (50 datasets)
other.value: TabPFN-3-Plus (Thinking) > TabPFN-3-Plus > text-aware baselines (CatBoost, TabSTAR, SAP-RPT-OSS); among numeric-only models TabPFN-3 is best

other.name: Causal inference (scikit-uplift QINI; RealCause PEHE)
other.value: TabPFN-3 as T- and S-learner tops the scikit-uplift uplift benchmark (up to 50k samples); slightly worse than TabPFN-2.5 on the small-sample RealCause benchmark

differences_vs_predecessor: Versus TabPFN-2.5 / TabPFN-2.6 (Nov 2025 / Mar 2026; 2.6 shares 2.5's architecture and limits with better benchmark scores): (1) new architecture - TabICLv2-style three-stage row compression (column-wise inducing-point embedding, row-wise CLS aggregation) feeding a 24-layer row-level ICL transformer, replacing 2.x's alternating row/feature attention; parameters grow from 11 M/10-13 M to 53 M/58 M; (2) attention-based many-class retrieval decoder: 160 classes natively instead of 10; (3) orthogonal label embeddings, RMSNorm instead of LayerNorm, explicit NaN/Inf indicators, QASSMax; (4) multi-query test attention shrinking the KV cache 8x (~7 GiB per estimator at 1M rows) and exact row-chunking, so 1M rows x 200 features run on a single H100 (2.5: 100k rows x 2,000 features) and inference is up to 20x faster; (5) preprocessing: GPU-side transforms, round-robin/balanced and Gini-importance feature subsampling, <=200 features per estimator (2.5: 500) with auto-scaled n_estimators, deterministic fingerprint hashing, SVD after categorical encoding; (6) richer SCM prior (new graph samplers, combiner mechanisms, categorical model, high-frequency oscillators, spatial, many-class, temporal dynamic-SCM and OOD priors) trained on >8T tokens; (7) results: TabArena Elo 1677 vs 1623 (TabPFN-2.6 D) and 1602 (RealTabPFN-2.5 T+E), regression improvements of up to 20% (docs), better OOD extrapolation, relational and time-series performance; slightly worse on the small-sample RealCause causal benchmark; (8) ecosystem: fine-tuning distributes over GPUs, regressor memory -60%, torch >= 2.5 required, API adds Thinking mode and native text (TabPFN-3-Plus) and a new /tabpfn/* endpoint surface; (9) licence: TABPFN-3 License v1.0 (non-commercial, like 2.5's v1.1 and 2.6's v1.0) [S1,S5,S9,S10].

notes: Variants: TabPFN-3-Plus (hosted API / VPC only; same interface; native free-text columns encoded jointly with numeric/categorical features; 1M rows x 2,000 columns) and TabPFN-3-Plus (Thinking) = TabPFN-3-Thinking (test-time compute spent at fit time, thinking_effort/thinking_metric parameters, up to 200k rows, up to ~15% Elo gain per docs; on TabArena 1800 Elo overall and 2146 on the medium subset, >200/420 Elo above every non-TabPFN model, beating AutoGluon 1.5 extreme (4h) by >100 Elo at <1/10 of its runtime; uses no LLMs, real data or other models; did not yet support temporal regression at publication) [S1,S9,S10]. TabPFN-TS-3: the tabpfn-v3-regressor-v3_20260506_timeseries.ckpt checkpoint fine-tuned on synthetic time series, default in tabpfn-time-series v1.1.0 (2026-05-12), 2nd on fev-bench behind Chronos-2 while trained on zero real series; the 20260417_binary/multiclass checkpoints are early (pre-full-pipeline) checkpoints used for the RelBench experiments [S1,S7,S16]. TabPFN-3 was superseded as default by TabPFN-3.5 (Sep 2026: single multitask checkpoint, 20k columns, local text support, Fast/Plus/Thinking variants); tabpfn-time-series moved to 3.5 in v1.3.0 [S4,S10,S16]. TabArena integration [S15]: wrapper uses the v3 default checkpoints, ignore_pretraining_limits=True, fixed random_state=0, max_classes=160, batched test inference above 150k rows, tabpfn>=8.0.8, 1 GPU required (10 GB baseline memory), 8-fold bagging + refit like other TFMs; registered with commercial_use=False ('TabPFN-3 License v1.0 (non-commercial)'), which drives the leaderboard's non-commercial marker; results were re-run on 2026-07-15 and 2026-09-16 timing pipelines. The Elo values quoted above are from the report's own TabArena run (May 2026 snapshot, TabPFN-3 on an RTX 6000) and will differ from the live leaderboard snapshot stored in data/tabarena.json. Open uncertainties: pre-training recipe (optimizer, steps, batch size, GPU-hours, curriculum), number of synthetic datasets and the definition of 'token', exact hard feature limit embedded in the checkpoint's InferenceConfig (docs/HF say 2,000; the report validates 20,000 features at 1k rows via feature subsampling), and the training loss. Parameter count is given per checkpoint (53 M classifier / 58 M regressor); parameters_m holds the classifier value.
